raw_response:
I am 73, my land is only 5 mu, and there are only 2 people in my household, so I will keep things simple and put my energy into the wheat-maize rotation that I already know well. That rotation fits my land, my experience, and my well irrigation, and it gives me steadier grain production with less risk and less labor than spreading myself too thin. Cotton takes more field management, more picking work, and more trouble with pests, so this year I will not give land to cotton. I will put all 5 mu into winter wheat first, then after wheat harvest I will plant summer maize on the same 5 mu. I will use improved seed for wheat because it is reliable and easy for me to manage, and hybrid seed for maize because I want stable output from a small area. I will fertilize moderately, irrigate when the crop most needs water, and keep pesticide use limited to what is needed. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical on a small farm and matches the way I would manage labor now.
